text:
ria: Hey team — Acme (enterprise) wants a 2-week POC starting next Mon. They want hosted API keys for developer access, a dedicated pool for load tests, and a VPC/private option for production-like testing. They also asked for a billing project with a hard spend cap + $5k trial credits. What are the feasible combos and potential blockers? @kai @annika @lucy

omar: Quick q — what's their peak qps and token mix? helps size the dedicated pool and estimate cost.

ria: Roughly 200 qps peak, typical prompt ~120 tokens, some long-context tests to 4k. They want failover to hosted if dedicated is saturated.

kai: Ok. Dedicated looks doable but provisioning GPU pool for ~200 qps + 4k context needs us to pick model/quantization. Timeline: can reserve a small pool in prod region in ~48h if capacity free, otherwise 5-7 days. Cheaper option: hosted with reserved concurrency + autoscale.

kai: On the VPC side — Private deployment (VPC) requires VPN or VPC peering and a brief network review. Security will need CIDR allowlist and egress controls. That adds 2-3 business days for network setup.

annika: Security notes — for a POC: we can use hosted keys with strict ingestion controls but if they insist on data staying in their VPC we need Private (customer-managed). Questions: do they need HSM/KMS integration? data residency?

lucy: Billing: we usually create a billing project for POCs (not full org) to keep spend scoped. We can apply $5k promo credits to that project and enable a hard spend cap via SpendShield (prepaid guard). For enterprise accounts we can also set a per-key quota. If they want a hard block, SpendShield is the reliable option.

ria: Great. Any gotchas re ephemeral keys for sales demos? we prefer ephemeral keys scoped to project with 24h expiry.

kai: Ephemeral keys are fine. For the dedicated->hosted fallback we can set routing policy: prefer dedicated, fall back to hosted model family. That requires a rollout config; simple YAML looks like:```
routing:
  primary: dedicated-pool:acme-poc
  fallback: hosted:gpt-4o-small
  fail_mode: fallback
```

ome: (typo) sorry, meant omar: Nice. How do we wire spend alerts? we should notify sales and infra before cap hit.

lucy: We can enable token-level alerts at 70% and 90% of credits plus webhook to #sales. Also enable automatic key disable on cap breach.

annika: If they require SOC2 evidence or SSO, that adds time. For SOC2/SSO we can provide standard attestation docs, but SSO/SCIM + role sync will take 3-5 days.

ria: Sounds like an action list. Can we confirm owners & ETA?

kai: I can own dedicated pool reservation + routing config. ETA: 48-72h if capacity available.

lucy: I'll create billing project, apply $5k promo, and enable SpendShield + alerts. ETA: same day. Need customer org ID and billing contact.

annika: I'll triage security checklist and confirm if HSM/KMS required. ETA: 24h. Need their SOC doc request form filled.

omar: I'll coordinate test plan with Acme (peak schedule, long-context scenarios) and hand over to Kai for sizing.

infra-bot: Project created: acme-poc-1717643210 — billing attached, promo-credit pending approval.

ria: Perfect. I'll message Acme for org ID, billing contact, and SSO/SOC requirements. Back here with updates. :thumbsup:

lucy: One more note — if dedicated provisioning delayed, we can start dev team on hosted keys with strict quotas so they can begin integration immediately.

ria: Good fallback. Thanks everyone — will update thread as we get customer details.
